sampling_model.design: For each fixed even \(m\), one-record laws belong to \(\mathcal H_{\beta,D}(m)\); the observed experiment is \(\mathbb P_{P,n}=\{P\circ(X,A,L)^{-1}\}^{\otimes n}\).
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent draws from the observed marginal of one fixed-\(m\) full-data law, with only \(X,A,L\) observed.
sampling_model.treatment: \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently of both potential losses conditional on \(X\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every observed cell-arm has known probability \(1/(2m)\); realized counts may be zero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: All \(2m\) survival tails are estimated from raw random-count samples by a total thresholded Hall procedure; no nuisance convergence rate is assumed.

Theorem 1 bounds constrained-policy regret for regular mean welfare by a policy-complexity and efficient-score scale.

body.tldr: Capacity-constrained treatment choice at a beyond-sample loss quantile is governed by the inverse of a selected heterogeneous survival mixture, not by separate cellwise extreme effects. For each fixed even cell count, the model is a nonempty Hall class and the data follow the observed marginal product experiment. The project derives the exact minimax expected logarithmic-regret frontier, identifies when capacity averaging strictly improves the coordinatewise Carpentier--Kim plug-in benchmark and why regular Athey--Wager complexity does not describe the tail loss, and constructs a computable sorting-and-inversion learner. A separate inference rung gives simultaneous policy intervals with selected-policy coverage as a corollary and attacks the sharp width converse through an explicit paired-cell Hall-splice hypercube.

project_justification.gap: Published quantile-policy methods supply fixed-level identification, one-tail Hall theory supplies a coordinatewise plug-in benchmark, and regular policy-learning theory supplies an additive-welfare complexity benchmark. None determines when capacity reallocation makes the exact heterogeneous mixture frontier strictly smaller than coordinatewise familywise control, nor the confidence-width modulus forced by paired Hall alternatives.
project_justification.niche: For each fixed even cell count, the randomized product experiment identifies every policy mixture and the capacity optimizer is computable by sorting, while local tail-index ties and randomly empty cells retain a nonregular decision problem.
project_justification.fill: The analysis combines a nonempty fixed-cell Hall class, exact soft mixture loss, and paired-splice testing to classify strict departures from both named regret baselines, then propagates bias-aware cell-tail regions through generalized inversion and matches them to a policy-mixture confidence-width converse.

body.related_work: WangZhouSongSherwood2018 already supplies the fixed-level policy-quantile identification logic, so identification is setup here; XiaZhangKong2026 develops successive classification for fixed quantile regimes. OsamaZachariahStoica2020 provides the matching upper-cost-quantile consumer, but its support-based conformal limit does not extrapolate an unbounded rare-loss tail. In CarpentierKim2015, the probability display in Theorem 3 gives the adaptive single-tail upper rate; equation (3.6) only imposes a lower requirement on the tuning constant \(A(\delta)\); and Theorem 4 separately gives the adaptive lower bound and its unavoidable log-log factor. Their relative parameter satisfies \(\beta_{\mathrm{CK}}=\beta/\alpha\) under the present absolute remainder envelope, so their exponent becomes \(\beta/(2\beta+\alpha)\) and its uniform worst case at \(\alpha=4\) is \(\varkappa=\beta/(2\beta+4)\). Familywise known-envelope calibration of this tail-event method and the threshold tools of BoucheronThomas2015 yield \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}\), whose strictness under capacity mixing is part of the frontier question. AtheyWager2021, specifically Theorem 1, and KitagawaTetenov2018 treat regular additive policy welfare; their \(\sqrt{m/n}\)-type complexity scale \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{AW}}\) is formally separated from moving extreme-tail regret. EinmahlHe2023 studies a predetermined heterogeneous average tail, PanovMorozova2021 studies vanishing heavy impurity, and DaouiaPadoanStupfler2024 studies common-tail pooling; none permits the decision rule to choose mixture components under capacity. SasakiWang2024 supplies a scalar worst-case-bias length principle, HuangLiPeng2025 supplies process inference for fixed treatment pairs and tail levels, and AndrewsKitagawaMcCloskey2024 supplies a regular winner-inference comparison; the explicit paired-cell Hall hypercube here instead forces separation among growing policy mixtures. GuggenbergerMehtaPavlov2026 studies bounded fixed-quantile minimax rules, while WangCaiWangShiTang2026 imposes a linear common-index structure for conditional extreme treatment effects.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The baseline paired-splice regret argument controls expected missed-cell count, but exact logarithmic loss is a concave log-sum-exp function of that count. Equal expected mistake counts can yield different expected regrets after unrestricted capacity reallocation, so a wrong-direction Jensen step cannot establish the sharp frontier. For confidence width, the displayed sign-indexed construction is only a route, and its quantitative implications remain unresolved.
body.honest_scope: Policy-mixture identification is fixed-level causal setup, not a novelty claim. The fixed-\(m\) Hall class, its exact-Pareto member, corrected \(m^{-1}\) sorting identity with the \(m=2\) arithmetic corollary, finite-policy inversion, Hall-core inversion, dominance map, generic regret sandwich, two-cell rate, and simultaneous confidence system are theorem claims. Selected-policy coverage is a corollary inside the simultaneous theorem. The exact many-cell regret question must classify its relations to both \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}\) and \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{AW}}\); the width question must analyze the displayed paired-splice experiment. No common tail index, fixed gap, density, continuous outcome law, nonempty realized cell sample, nuisance-estimator rate, or selection penalty is assumed.
